english.title: Religious hatred - direct public performance of play intending to stir up
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) directed the public performance of a play, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PLAY..), which involved the use of threatening words or behaviour, intending thereby to stir up religious hatred
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 29D(1) and 29L(3) of the Public Order Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
directed the public performance of a play which involved the use of threatening words/behaviour
intending to stir up religious hatred

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording is now OBSOLETE. Now see CJS Code PU86140 and H6662. Option re "Sexual orientation" added by Sch 16 to the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008 as from 23/03/2010.

(i) Section 29D(2) of the Public Order Act 1986 exempts from the offence under certain circumstances a performance given solely or primarily for one or more of the following purposes rehearsal, making a recording of the performance, or
enabling the performance to be included in a programme service.
(ii) Section 29D(5) of the Act provides that the following provisions of the Theatres Act 1968 apply in relation to this offence as they apply to an offence under section 2 of that Act
section 9 (script as evidence of what was performed),
section 10 (power to make copies of script),
section 15 ( powers of entry and inspection).
(iii) The consent of the Attorney General is required for prosecution of this offence.
(iv) See also H8424 'present public performance of play intending to stir up racial hatred'.
(v) Section 29L(2) of the Public Order Act 1986 provides that for purposes of the rules in England and Wales against charging more than one offence in the same count or information, each of sections 29B to 29G creates one offence.
(vi) This offence was inserted into the Public Order Act 1986 by the Racial and Religious Hatred Act 2006.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.
